comparison: Both strongly support the superior barrier properties of the triple co-culture model (C2-C4, C37-C57). OpenEval provides detailed analysis of TEER, permeability, protein expression, and correlation studies. Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed these findings with all three reviewers confirming the model 'recapitulates key aspects' and 'well mimicked several important characteristics of BBB.' High agreement on core barrier function claims.

Both strongly support GDNF as the key mediator from neurons/astrocytes (C5-C8, C58-C75). OpenEval emphasizes systematic testing and neutralization data. Peer reviewers explicitly confirmed the mechanism was 'Convincingly' described and that 'experiments and data presented support the claim.' Complete agreement on GDNF identification and role.

Both support the GDNF signaling mechanism through pharmacological inhibition (C9-C12, C76-C86). OpenEval highlights the use of multiple inhibitors and functional consequences. Peer reviewers affirmed the mechanism is 'Convincingly' described and that neurons/astrocytes act through GDNF secretion. Strong concordance on signaling pathway validation.

Both support the PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK pathway activation by GDNF (C13-C14, C87-C95). OpenEval emphasizes pathway specificity through inhibitor studies. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly stated mechanisms were 'meticulously conducted' with 'conclusions firmly supported by the data.' Complete agreement on downstream signaling pathways.

Both support FOXO1-mediated claudin-5 regulation via PI3K/AKT (C96-C109). OpenEval details multiple complementary approaches including siRNA and overexpression. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of the overall mechanistic pathway that was 'meticulously conducted.' No challenges raised; strong agreement on FOXO1 mechanism.

Both support ETS1-mediated VE-cadherin regulation requiring both PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK (C15-C16, C113-C121, C163-C166). OpenEval emphasizes specificity for VE-cadherin versus claudin-5. Peer reviewers accepted this differential regulation without challenge as part of the validated mechanistic pathway. Complete concordance.

Both strongly support in vivo validation using AAV-mediated GDNF knockdown (C17, C122-C131). OpenEval emphasizes consistency with in vitro findings and specificity of brain knockdown. All three peer reviewers explicitly affirmed the in vivo validation, with editor stating authors 'demonstrated that knock-down of this neurotrophic factor, increased the permeability.' Perfect agreement on in vivo validation.

Both support the model's utility for CNS drug permeability prediction (C18, C20, C132-C136, C169-C170, C178). OpenEval emphasizes systematic testing of 18 drugs and appropriate acknowledgment of failures. Peer reviewers confirmed the model 'demonstrated predictive value' and is 'a valuable tool for high throughput screening.' Strong agreement on practical applications.

Both support the explanation for prediction failures with highly protein-bound drugs (C171-C176). OpenEval notes this demonstrates scientific rigor in acknowledging limitations. Peer reviewers accepted this explanation without challenge as a known issue with fu,brain measurements. Agreement on limitation acknowledgment.

Both support that proliferation alone cannot account for improved barrier properties (C45-C47). OpenEval emphasizes the control experiment distinguishing proliferation-dependent versus independent mechanisms. Peer reviewers accepted this control without challenge. Agreement on mechanistic distinction.

Both support the negative finding that VE-cadherin silencing does not affect claudin-5 (C110-C112). OpenEval notes this suggests cell-type-specific differences and is important for understanding independence of regulation. Peer reviewers accepted this negative result without requesting additional experiments. Agreement on independent regulation.

Both support the main conclusions and summary statements (C19, C177, C179). OpenEval characterizes these as appropriate concluding statements. All peer reviewers affirmed the main conclusions with statements that the study 'presents valuable evidence' and 'conclusions are firmly supported by the data.' Complete agreement on overall conclusions.

Both address U251 cells as physical barrier contributors (C40, C42). OpenEval includes this in comprehensive barrier property analysis, noting it's appropriately acknowledged. Peer reviewers accepted this as supporting data for model characterization without challenge. Agreement on physical barrier contribution.

Overlap on qPCR data (C48). OpenEval groups this with neurotrophic factor rationale as supporting observations. Peer reviewers include this in their affirmation of the model's barrier properties. Minor overlap; both accept the data without challenge.

Overlap on neuronal GDNF secretion evidence (C146-C150, C148-C150). OpenEval notes the inference is reasonable but somewhat indirect using neuroblastoma cells. Peer reviewers affirmed neurons release GDNF as part of the overall mechanism. Agreement on GDNF source, though OpenEval notes limitation of cell line model.

Partial overlap on TEER values and model limitations (C137-C145, C39-C141). OpenEval characterizes literature citations as appropriate context. Peer reviewers explicitly noted as UNCERTAIN that TEER values remain lower than physiological levels and suggested future enhancement methods. Divergence: OpenEval accepts as context, peer reviewers flag as limitation requiring future work.

Overlap on future directions and limitations (C180). OpenEval characterizes this as appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly noted as UNCERTAIN the lack of pericyte interactions, though acknowledged the model is 'enough to study BBB permeability.' Divergence: OpenEval accepts as appropriate limitation statement, peer reviewers flag as specific gap requiring future attention.

OpenEval evaluated background/literature context claims (C1, C21-C36) as SUPPORTED, noting they establish appropriate rationale from established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims specifically.

OpenEval evaluated extensive discussion/literature context claims (C137-C145, C151-C162, C167-C168) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citation of relevant literature and balanced interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for most of these discussion claims, though peer reviewers did flag specific limitations (see R14, R15 peer results).
